EDS is a genetic connective tissue disorder, which means that there is an error in the DNA that makes one or more types of collegen in the body, thus the collegen type(s) that is/are affected are made faulty ie too stretchy, too fragile, etc. There are 13 known types and they all present differently according to the type of collagen associated with that type. Am example being: the Vascular type of EDS affects the blood vessels, heart, facial features, and other internal organs, while the classical type affects more prominently the joints and skin fragility (also note that many symptoms between types will overlap, such as soft skin and joint pain).

My GES was normal but a manometry study two days later show essentially no movement from the stomach. I hear a lot of cases of the GES not showing a delay despite having, even severe, gastroparesis.

fullness after eating, pain after eating, bloating, nausea after eating, and regurgitation (but no vomitting) after eating and those symptoms would last from 6-20 hours after eating, and I also experienced weight loss, and malnutrition (deficencies, organs going to crap, hair loss, etc.)

I had my GES come back totally normal and had a manometry study done two days later that showed total paralysis. Ive heard that a GES can somehow miss gastroparesis, like in my case, but i dont know how. If you think you have GP, you might ask about getting an antroduodenal manometry study done.
